lbl.Gli strati accesi compaiono come eti: Active layers appear as labels at the top of the map and the legend at the bottom left explains their colours. Next to each layer, buttons let you move it up or down, centre the map on its data and change its colours; the “Search layer” field filters the list. You can turn on more than one to compare them, for example buildings and cadastre.
lbl.Gli strati molto densi (come le part: Very dense layers (such as cadastral parcels) look better with WMS: WFS download has a cap of 10,000 features.
lbl.Gli strati si ricordano da una visit: Layers are remembered from one visit to the next, in this browser. If a service stops responding, it stays in the list marked as “unavailable” and is not deleted.
lbl.Gli strati sono i temi che si posson: Layers are the themes that can be overlaid on the map. On the left a vertical bar has five tabs: “Basemap”, “Layers”, “RNDT”, “My layers” and “Filters”. The “Layers” tab opens a panel with the groups of layers (Boundaries, Buildings, Events, Monuments, PAI plan, Population, Terrain, Services, Road safety, Territory, Transport), always in alphabetical order: a click on the group opens it, and each layer has a box to turn it on or off. The panel stays open until you press the tab again or Esc; on a smartphone it opens from the “Layers” tab, while “My layers”, the RNDT catalogue and Geoimage are in the “Add” tab.

lbl.Il pulsante con la tabella, nella ba: The table button, in the toolbar at the top right, opens the “Data table” from the bottom: the rows of the active layers, one tab per layer, like an attribute table. It shows the information loaded in the current view, so moving or zooming the map updates it; on a smartphone the button is in the “Layers” sheet. A layer that is switched off has no tab.
lbl.Per scegliere cosa vedere ci sono qu: Four selection tools choose what to see: “Click” picks one feature, “Box” and “Polygon” pick those inside the area you draw, “Area” picks those inside a district, a neighbourhood or a UPL. “Back to the view” returns to the rows visible on the map. The “Filter the rows” field searches the text, the column heading sorts, and the “Columns” menu shows, hides and moves columns.
lbl.Le caselle scelgono righe e colonne: The checkboxes choose the rows and columns to export; the CSV or GeoJSON button shows how many rows and columns will be written (for example “33 × 15”) and adds the layer's source and licence. Export is enabled for the City's open data whose licence allows it, such as road accidents and road safety; for the other layers, and for those you add yourself, the button stays off. The geometry of tiled layers is simplified: for precise data use the CSV.

lbl.Ogni linea del trasporto pubblico (b: Every public transport line (AMAT buses and trams, the urban railway metro) opens from the profile: turn on the “Bus lines”, “Tram lines” or “Metro line” layers and click on the route or on a stop. In the “Lines” box you pick the line and, in its block, open “Stops”: the stops appear in sequence as a strip diagram, with the line in its own colour, a dot for each stop and the terminals larger and in bold.
lbl.Accanto al nome di ogni fermata, i r: Next to the name of each stop, the coloured boxes with a number are the other lines that serve it: the interchanges. A click on a box takes the map to the stop and shows the route of that line; a click on the name takes the map to the stop and opens its profile, with the next departures. If you click on a stop rather than on the route, its lines open anyway with the same diagram. A terminus with arrivals only says so: no trips leave from there and the timetable is at the departure stop.
lbl.La mappa con il tracciato e le ferma: The map with the route and stops of line 442 and, in the profile, the “Stops (19)” block: the stops in sequence on a coloured strip, with the boxes of the other lines serving them beside each name.

lbl.Il pulsante con l'omino, nella barra: The little-person button, in the toolbar at the top right, switches Street View on: the cursor becomes a crosshair. Press on the point of the map you are interested in and, holding down, drag to choose the viewing direction; a blue cone shows where the panorama will look.
lbl.Al rilascio si apre una finestra con: On release a window opens with the Google Street View panorama of the point: move it by dragging the top bar, resize it from the corner and close it with the cross. “Open in Google Maps” opens it full screen in a new tab. lbl.Nella barra di destra il tab «Tema»: The «Theme» tab (the palette) in the right-hand bar opens the panel that changes the look of the whole application, not just the map. At the top are the «Ready-made themes», each with its own thumbnail: Light, Dark, High contrast and many more. One click applies a theme straight away, with a live preview, and your choice is kept in this browser.
lbl.Sotto i temi si regolano a mano i ci: Below the themes you can set the five base colours by hand: background, text, accent, link and borders. If a colour is hard to read on the background, a warning shows the measured contrast and the recommended minimum. «Advanced colours» also lets you choose the status colours (positive result, error and alarm, background of notices), the colour of the searched parcel and the colour of values in charts. The «Text» section changes the size and the typeface, including Atkinson Hyperlegible, designed for high legibility.
lbl.«Salva su file» scrive il tema in un: «Save to file» writes the theme to a file on your computer, which «Load from file» can read back, even on another device: it is not sent to anyone. «Restore standard colours» removes the custom theme, as does the light/dark button in the toolbar.
pres.perche.dt.p1: It starts from the opposite question: "What is here?"
pres.perche.dt.p2: A single map, many layers you switch on and off: cadastre, zoning plan, population, buildings, relief, public transport, heat islands, hydrogeological risk, monuments, historical maps, municipal offices and more. One click on a point and the place card opens, bringing together all the data for that address.
pres.perche.dt.p3: But it is not only for looking, it is for working. Students, professionals and technicians can bring their own data onto the map and use it together with the layers already there, as in QGIS: just connect a source or drag a file, with nothing to install.
pres.perche.hub.p1: Each map is a work in its own right, with its own theme, source, author and year.
pres.perche.hub.p2: It works very well when the question is: "Is there a map on this topic?"
pres.perche.hub.p4: The limit is structural: each map lives on its own. To know what happens at a precise point of the city (which cadastral parcel it is, which zoning of the PRG, whether there are hydrogeological constraints, how hot it gets in summer) you have to open several maps, in several tabs, and compare the results by hand.

lbl.Sui layer a punti il colore non è l': On point layers colour is not the only cue: each layer has its own shape or icon, the same on the map, in the legend and in the hover box. MEF properties show a euro icon, and architectural barriers have one icon per group (historic route, city street, square, green area, museum…). Schools, polling stations, fuel stations, charging points, drinking fountains and monumental trees show a graduation cap, a check mark, a pump, a plug, a drop and a tree, in the colour of the type, brand or status. Municipal office sites carry a building icon at the centre of the ring: the bigger it is, the more offices it hosts. Monuments have one icon per category: church, colonnade, theatre, house, building, palette, book, tree, market, ruins, shield or pin. Accidents, stops and commuting stay circles. This keeps themes apart when printing in black and white or with colour-vision difficulties.
lbl.Il pulsante con il fumetto, nella ba: The speech-bubble button in the toolbar at the top right, or the “Talia” tab of the right-hand bar, opens Talia, the assistant that answers questions about the app, its layers and its functions. You type the question in the field at the bottom and press “Send”; on opening, Talia also offers a few questions to tap. Answers do not come from an external service: they are drawn from the site’s guide, in the language of the app, and above each answer is the title of the entry it comes from. “Read more” expands a long answer; if it finds nothing, Talia says so and suggests similar questions; the bin button clears the conversation.
lbl.Sotto la risposta compaiono dei puls: Below the answer there are buttons that let you act without searching the menus. A button with a layer’s name, such as “Charging points”, turns that layer on or off. When the layer has filters, the filter buttons appear, grouped (for the charging points: “Status” with “Available”, “Charging” and “Inactive”; “Current” with “Alternating current (AC, slow)” and “Direct current (DC, fast)”): one click leaves only that item on the map, “Show all” removes every filter. Choosing items from different groups leaves only the elements that meet all of them; the “On the map” line sums up the active filters and the legend on the map updates accordingly. Other buttons open the sheet of a place that was found, a panel tab or the related guide entry.
lbl.A sinistra la mappa con lo strato Co: On the left the map with the Charging points layer on and only the available chargers highlighted; on the right the Talia panel with the answer about charging points, the layer button and the “Status” and “Current” filter buttons, with “Available” pressed and the line “On the map: Status: Available”.

info.barre.titolo: Earthquakes per day, month or year
info.barre.cosa: How many earthquakes there were each day, month or year in Italy. Each bar is a period: the taller it is, the more events.
info.barre.come: It uses INGV data for the last 5 years, from magnitude 2 up (below that there would be tens of thousands of events). The «Events per» menu picks the unit: 30 days, 24 months or 5 years. A bar turns red when it has far more events than usual: the threshold is the median of the bars plus 4 times the median deviation (never under 6 events), so swarms do not raise it themselves. Consecutive red bars are merged in the «Swarms and seismic sequences» list.
info.barre.leggere: Hover a bar to see the date, the number of events and the maximum magnitude. A lone red bar is a swarm; several red bars in a row are a seismic sequence.
info.mt.cosa: Every earthquake in the chosen window, placed along time: the height of the stem is the magnitude.
info.mt.come: Time runs on the horizontal axis (same window as the bars), magnitude on the vertical one. The strongest shock in the window, the mainshock, is in red with its label; the events after it are the possible aftershocks. Clicking a stem opens the event on the map and in the panel.
info.mt.leggere: A tall shock followed by many short stems is the classic sequence with aftershocks. Tall stems scattered in time, with no main shock, are independent events.
info.cum.cosa: The running total of events as time goes by.
info.cum.come: The curve starts at 0 and goes up by one for every earthquake in the window (M ≥ the chosen threshold); the vertical axis reaches the total. It does not count how strong the events are, only how many.
info.cum.leggere: The slope is the pace of activity. Flat stretch: quiet period. Steep climb: many events close together. A change of slope signals an increase (or a drop) in activity; an almost vertical jump is a swarm or a run of aftershocks.
info.omori.cosa: How a seismic sequence dies out: how many aftershocks occurred each day after the strongest shock.
info.omori.come: The mainshock is the strongest shock in the window. From then on events are counted in whole 24-hour days (the current, incomplete day is left out). Both axes are logarithmic (1, 10, 100…) and days with no aftershocks cannot be drawn. The dashed line is the least-squares fit n ∝ t^−p, i.e. Omori's law; it needs at least 3 days with aftershocks.
info.omori.leggere: If the points follow a straight line, the sequence decays regularly. The value p is the slope: close to 1 is a typical decay, higher means it dies out faster. With few aftershocks the estimate is rough and it is not a forecast.
info.pf-tempo.cosa: The number of earthquakes on each of the last 30 days, with the option to choose which ones to show on the map.
info.pf-tempo.come: Each bar is a day; the count respects the minimum magnitude and the classes switched on. The two-handle slider picks the range: the map, the menus and the list show only the events of those days. «Play» moves the window one day at a time, «Reset» goes back to the whole period.
info.pf-tempo.leggere: Tall bars are the most active days: moving the slider there shows where the events cluster.
info.pf-magnitudo.cosa: How many earthquakes there are in each magnitude class: 1–2, 2–3, 3–4 and 4 or more.
info.pf-magnitudo.come: The number above each column counts the events in the chosen time range. Clicking a column switches that class on or off on the map and in the other charts.
info.pf-magnitudo.leggere: Weak earthquakes are far more numerous than strong ones: the columns normally shrink towards high magnitudes.
terremoti.energia.nota: Seismic moment accumulated by {n} events, as a percentage of the total. The strongest (M {forte}) alone weighs {quota}%. The whole release equals a single earthquake of M {mag}.
terremoti.attese.nota: {n} waits between one event and the next; median wait {mediana}; coefficient of variation {cv}. Near 1 events arrive at random; higher, they are clustered in swarms. Waits under a day are in red.
terremoti.st.nota: {n} events: time horizontally, latitude vertically; the bigger the circle, the stronger the magnitude. The strongest is in red. A click opens the event.
info.energia.cosa: How much seismic energy was released in the window, accumulated over time, as a percentage of the total.
info.energia.come: Each earthquake weighs according to its seismic moment, which grows about 32 times per magnitude unit (Hanks and Kanamori relation, M0 = 10^(1.5·M + 9.1) N·m). The curve adds these values over time and reaches 100%. In the note, the equivalent magnitude is that of a single earthquake that would have released the whole total. Magnitudes are INGV's, of mixed types: the result is an approximation.
info.energia.leggere: While the count is dominated by the many small events, here the few large ones matter: a tall step is a strong shock. If the curve is almost one single jump, one event released nearly all the energy even if there are hundreds of events.
info.attese.cosa: How much time passes between one earthquake and the next, to tell swarms from background activity.
info.attese.come: The events in the window are put in time order and the wait between each neighbouring pair is measured. Waits are grouped in classes, from under a minute to over a year. Classes under a day are in red. The coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by the mean) is about 1 if events arrive at random.
info.attese.leggere: Many short waits and a few very long ones, with a coefficient well above 1, mean clustered events: swarms and aftershocks. Waits spread over several classes, with a coefficient near 1, mean background activity. With few events the shape is unreliable.
info.spaziotempo.cosa: Where and when the earthquakes happened: time runs left to right, latitude from south (bottom) to north (top).
info.spaziotempo.come: Each circle is an earthquake at its latitude; size follows magnitude and red marks the strongest. The vertical axis runs from the lowest to the highest latitude of the events shown. It is latitude, not distance along a fault, because the app does not know the fault orientation.
info.spaziotempo.leggere: A group of circles drifting diagonally, up or down, is a migrating swarm. A single cloud staying on one row is a sequence that stays in the same place.
terremoti.omori.nota: Aftershocks per day after the strongest shock (M {forte}, {data}), on logarithmic axes. The dashed line is the fit n ∝ t^−p: p = {p}. Values of p near 1 are typical of a normally decaying sequence; the higher it is, the faster it dies out.

lbl.Luoghi di prima accoglienza per la p: First-reception places for the population: squares, open spaces, car parks, public or private areas not exposed to risk (away from landslides, floods, collapsing structures), reachable by a safe route. Here people receive the first information on the event and the first comforts, for a period from a few hours to a few days. Source: Civil Protection Glossary.
lbl.Luoghi in aree sicure, vicini a riso: Places in safe areas, close to water, power and sewage services, where the first housing settlements are set up to shelter the affected population. They must be easy to reach, even for large vehicles, so they can be set up and managed. Accommodation facilities (hotels, residences, campsites) may also be included. Source: Civil Protection Glossary.
lbl.Zone sicure rispetto ai rischi, dove: Zones safe from the risks, where rescuers and the resources needed for a rational response in the emergency areas find suitable accommodation. They must be easy to reach by safe routes, even for large vehicles, and close to water and power supplies, with wastewater disposal. Stays in an emergency last from a few weeks to a few months. Source: Civil Protection Glossary.
lbl.La presenza sul territorio di stabil: Industrial plants that use or hold chemical substances expose the population and the environment to industrial risk: an accident can injure people and damage the environment. The effects depend on the substances' characteristics, concentration and exposure time. Knowing these aspects helps reduce the risk to a minimum. Source: Civil Protection Glossary.

lbl.In questa modalità il tocco non apre: In this mode a tap does not open the pop-up on the map but **only the card of that area**, full height, without the other information about the point. The card gives the **type of area** and its **number**, the **surface area** and where it is (**district, neighbourhood, UPL**).
lbl.Il pulsante verde **«Apri nel naviga: The green **«Open in navigator»** button opens the phone's navigation app with the **route already set** to the area: start the directions and **follow the road**.
lbl.La scheda di un'area di ammassamento: The card of a rescuers' assembly area, with number and surface, district, neighbourhood and UPL, the green «Open in navigator» button and the numbers 112, 115, 118, 113 and 1515.
lbl.Nella scheda premi «Apri nel navigat: In the card press «Open in navigator» and let yourself be guided.
lbl.In emergenza **valgono sempre le ind: In an emergency, **the instructions of Civil Protection and the authorities always prevail**.
lbl.La parte bassa della scheda con i nu: The lower part of the card with the Civil Protection and regional operations room numbers, the official websites and the small map with the chosen area highlighted in pink.
lbl.Numeri utili, siti ufficiali e la ma: Useful numbers, official websites and the map of the chosen area.
